archetype: WU forced-draw punisher control with a hug-fort shell and a VERIFIED storm-kill finisher — and tutor-backed access to it: symmetric table-draw engines feeding asymmetric hand-size punishers, Heliod, the Warped Eclipse converting opponents' draws into cost reduction and flash, the checker-passed Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + Arcane Signet + Aetherflux Reservoir table-kill as the primary win line, Grand Abolisher as its purpose-built protection, a four-walker sweep-surviving second layer, and Enlightened Tutor buying instant-speed consistency for every artifact/enchantment piece of the kill

role_assignment.default_role: control with inevitability: the punisher upkeep damage (verified stack 003: Iron Maiden + Ebony Owl Netsuke deal 7 on the punished upkeep once Forced Fruition fills the hand; cleanup trims to exactly 7) is a clock that runs without tapping out, and the interaction suite — Archmage's Charm among it, held by t6 in 67.2% of goldfish games (77.8% ever) — defends the long game. Whoever loses the long game must be the beatdown, and that is usually not you (strategy:whos-the-beatdown, strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). The hug-fort layer (Kwain, The Second Doctor) buys the waiting turns politically (strategy:multiplayer.politics), and Teferi, Hero of Dominaria lets you advance the clock while holding counter mana — his +1 draws and untaps two lands at the next end step
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: the go decision is concrete storm arithmetic (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math): commit the turn you can deploy Hullbreaker Horror plus both rocks and Aetherflux Reservoir in one main phase — ideally the turn after Grand Abolisher, whose static closes every priority window the verified kill (stack 006) honestly opens — or the turn Approach of the Second Sun's second cast is set up behind held countermagic (verified stack 002). Enlightened Tutor sharpens the trigger: at instant speed on the end step before your commit turn it puts any artifact/enchantment piece of the kill (Reservoir, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Thought Vessel — everything but Hullbreaker itself) on top for your draw, converting a three-of-four board into a scheduled four-of-four (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors). Hold protection FOR the commit turn, not after (strategy:pivot-point); going early into three players' open mana is how the 15-cast line dies (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). Wincon access is 49.6% of goldfish games by t6 (61.2% ever, mean turn 3.207) with Enlightened Tutor in the access group

engines.piece: Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + Arcane Signet + Aetherflux Reservoir
engines.engine: THE VERIFIED PRIMARY WIN LINE. Stack 006 (checker: pass) walks the complete table-kill with an exact ledger: the 004-verified mana-neutral alternating-bounce loop makes each cast n net +n life off the Reservoir's 'you gain 1 life for each spell you've cast this turn' (triangular growth); from 32 life, 15 casts is the proven minimum funding three 'Pay 50 life: deal 50 damage' activations that kill all three opponents in one main phase via SBAs, ending at 2 life with the loop still available. The verified weakness in the same artifact: every activation and every loop cast opens a fully open priority window — the engine gives itself zero protection. Requires nothing beyond the four pieces and {2} to start. The loop is not tied to any one rock: the 004-verified engine is Hullbreaker + Sol Ring + a two-mana any-colour rock, and Thought Vessel ({T}: Add {C}) qualifies exactly
engines.evidence: verified stack 006 (data/decks/heliod/stacks/006-aetherflux-storm-lethal.json); verified stack 004 (data/decks/heliod/stacks/004-hullbreaker-three-card-engine.json — loop mana-neutral, unbounded); verified stack 001 (data/decks/heliod/stacks/001-hullbreaker-sol-ring-loop.json — two-card form REFUTED); verified stack 005 (data/decks/heliod/stacks/005-displacer-kitten-mana-positive.json — Kitten mana-positive extension REFUTED); oracle text (Aetherflux Reservoir, Thought Vessel)

engines.engine: the consistency engine and the deck's tenth Game Changer: 'Search your library for an artifact or enchantment card, reveal it, then shuffle and put that card on top' — at instant speed for {W}. It reaches every artifact/enchantment piece of the verified kill (Aetherflux Reservoir, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Thought Vessel) — everything but Hullbreaker Horror, the one creature — plus the punisher core (Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke, Forced Fruition), the taxes and doublers (Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe, Alhammarret's Archive), and Propaganda. Per the tutors-as-copies frame, k tutors plus a card act like k+1 copies of every card in the deck (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors) — one slot backs up the kill, the punisher two-piece, and the value layer simultaneously. Honest cost: it tops, not draws — the piece arrives a draw step later unless a draw engine picks it up, which this deck of Howling Mines usually provides; and it cannot fetch Hullbreaker or Approach (sorcery)
engines.evidence: oracle text (Enlightened Tutor); bracket_report.json (tenth Game Changer, floor 4); goldfish 'Win condition access' group membership, 49.6% by t6, 61.2% ever

engines.piece: Grand Abolisher + the free/cheap counter suite (Archmage's Charm included)
engines.engine: the protection layer the verified kill does not provide itself. Stack 006's honest caveat is that the kill's windows are rules-open on an unprotected board; Grand Abolisher's 'During your turn, your opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments' closes exactly those windows on exactly the turn the loop runs. Sequencing rule: Abolisher the turn before, or lead the commit turn with him; failing that, the suite (Fierce Guardianship, Force of Negation, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Dovin's Veto, Counterspell, Arcane Denial, and Archmage's Charm) guards the windows the hard way — held-protection-on-the-commit-turn made literal (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). The suite runs deep: Charm's three modes (counter, draw two, steal a mana-value-1-or-less permanent — an opposing Sol Ring) make it interaction that is never dead, the flexible-answer discipline the interaction-suite school prescribes (strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite). Goldfish 'Free or cheap interaction held' is 67.2% by t6. Unverified caveat carried from the sideboard analysis: the Abolisher-closes-006 claim has no checker-passed walkthrough, and Otawara-style channel abilities activate from hand, outside Abolisher's list
engines.evidence: oracle text (Grand Abolisher, Archmage's Charm); verified stack 006 names Abolisher as the in-99 window-closer; goldfish 'Free or cheap interaction held' 67.2% by t6, 77.8% ever, mean turn 2.729

engines.piece: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria + Jace Beleren + Jace, Wielder of Mysteries + Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim
engines.engine: the sweep-surviving threat layer, four walkers deep: they dodge Supreme Verdict — including YOUR OWN — so you can wrath a hostile board while your threats keep drawing. This is Duke's 'buy resilience instead of restraint' answer to sweeper exposure (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). Teferi, Hero of Dominaria is the layer's centrepiece: his +1 draws AND untaps two lands at the next end step — a clock that advances while your counter mana stays open, exactly the posture this deck wants — his -3 is repeatable tuck removal that also answers stax lock pieces, and his -8 emblem exiles a permanent per draw in a deck built on drawing. Beleren's +2 feeds the punisher math and Heliod's discount; Temporal Pilgrim self-charges off every draw; Wielder of Mysteries is a standing wincon whose +1 draws while threatening the empty-library win
engines.evidence: oracle text (all four walkers, Supreme Verdict); goldfish 'Win condition access' 49.6% by t6, 61.2% ever

With the kill verified through the Reservoir, the Kitten's job is value, not combo

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: In the control mirror someone must be the beatdown (strategy:whos-the-beatdown) — and your punishers advance during draw-go, so you own inevitability (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). The sweep layering is deep: FOUR walkers live through every Supreme Verdict, including yours (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math), and Teferi, Hero of Dominaria is the mirror's best card — his +1 advances the clock while the end-step untap keeps two counter-lands open, and Archmage's Charm's draw-two mode means your held interaction is never dead in a permission stalemate (strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite). Real exposure remains artifact/enchantment mass removal taking engine and punisher layers together, plus Hullbreaker dying to creature wraths; keep the kill pieces in hand until the commit turn (strategy:pivot-point) — Enlightened Tutor at their end step makes that discipline cheap. Supreme Verdict is YOUR uncounterable reset through their permission.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes attack this deck's velocity math — many cheap spells per turn — so recount the hand under the tax (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial); under an assembling lock your role flips to beatdown, racing completion. Heliod's per-opponent-draw discount is a partial tax rebate the forced-draw engines keep feeding; Kitten re-triggering Loran and Teferi Hero's -3 tucking a lock piece give repeatable answers. You are partly the denial player yourself: Drannith Magistrate shuts off opponents' commanders and every non-hand cast. The 15-cast kill needs only {2} and the pieces: it races most soft locks that don't stop artifact casts — and Enlightened Tutor finds the missing piece through a resource-starved board.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Propaganda and The Second Doctor's attack-deterrent rider (plus Eiganjo's channel removal) are virtual card advantage tripled in multiplayer — one pillow effect blanks attack plans from three players (strategy:card-advantage.virtual) — but note honestly: the deck runs two attack taxes, with Ghostly Prison in the sideboard — a bet that never-dead interaction (Archmage's Charm) beats a redundant third tax at a professional table. The punishers convert defense into a clock that pushes the aggressor's damage-per-card below lethal (strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire). Commit little and let them overextend into Supreme Verdict (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). The trap remains: Forced Fruition refuels their hand — sequence punishers before or with the big draw engines (strategy:critical-mass). Life-total caveat: the Reservoir kill pays 50 life three times; stack 006 proves any positive total works because per-cast gain grows without bound, but lower totals need more casts and therefore more open windows.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Hold the suite (Fierce Guardianship, Force of Negation, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Dovin's Veto, Counterspell, Arcane Denial, Archmage's Charm — held by t6 in 67.2% of goldfish games) for the card that ends the game, per the answer-economy bar (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). Drannith Magistrate blanks commander- and non-hand-zone lines before they start; Grand Abolisher makes YOUR combo turn uninterruptable (unverified at the edges — see the Abolisher candidate); and Enlightened Tutor at instant speed means you can hold interaction AND assemble — the tutor-as-extra-copy math working under pressure (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors). You are the faster, better-protected combo deck in many pods, which flips your role to beatdown (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). Standing warning: Forced Fruition hands a storm pilot seven cards per spell; expect tables to discount your quiet artifacts and hit you anyway (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).

distribution_notes: 85 entries / 100 copies, 18 land entries (33 land copies); curve 9/21/15/11 at MV 1-4 with eleven cards at MV 5+, leaning on Heliod's discount for the top end. Pips skew hard blue: 61 U pips across 40 cards (source target 36 vs 6 U-producing lands — rocks and duals carry it) against 16 W pips across 14 (target 22, 11 W lands). The UUU cost is real and named: Archmage's Charm is the deck's only triple-pip card, and Karsten's table wants 37 U sources to cast {U}{U}{U} on curve at ~90% (strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources) — the deck sits at a 36-source target, so treat Charm as a t4+ spell cast off duals and Heliod's discount, not a t3 promise. Goldfish (seed 42, 10k iters, sha 284067d77208): commander mean cast 4.161 (median 4, 89.6% by t6), keep-first-seven 73.4%; table draw engine 76.2% by t6; core two-piece 41.3% by t6 (56.6% ever); wincon access 49.6% by t6 (61.2% ever); interaction held 67.2% by t6. Mulligan rule: engine-half hands dig toward punishers; punisher-only hands are blanks until the engine exists (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands). Bracket floor 4 (Optimized) on TEN Game Changers — Enlightened Tutor is the tenth — plus the two-card-infinite signal; stack 001 refuted that listed line but stack 006 verifies the four-card table-kill, so the floor-4 conversation stays honest either way.
overall_assessment: This deck pairs a verified kill with tutor-backed access to it. The world-view is still Duke's inevitability (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock): every symmetric draw is asymmetric three ways — Heliod's discount, the hand-size punishers, the Tithe/Sphinx value layer — the hug-fort keeps the waiting game political (strategy:multiplayer.politics), and the endgame is the checker-passed 15-cast Reservoir ledger (stack 006) behind Grand Abolisher (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math, strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). Three cards carry that identity at a tier-4 table: Enlightened Tutor turns the four-piece kill from a draw problem into a one-mana instant plus a draw step — it fetches every piece but Hullbreaker, and the punisher core besides (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors); Teferi, Hero of Dominaria is the sweep-surviving clock that holds its counter mana open while it ticks (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math); Archmage's Charm is interaction that is never dead — the deck carries its attack tax twice already, and Ghostly Prison sits in the sideboard as a third. The honestly-named tensions: a heavy blue pip load against a 36-source target, a lean rock suite (loop-safe — Thought Vessel is the 004 engine's exact substitute), and a two-effect pillow layer. Play it as the control deck that never has to win the long game it owns — and the moment Enlightened Tutor schedules the fourth piece behind an Abolisher, stop playing fair (strategy:pivot-point).
